author: embirico
text:
8/8: Conclusion
- Only a day in, but this launch might be more about internet presence than immediate results.
- As a leader, the hardest part is figuring out the most productive framing for the team.
- Proud of team for rallying. Excited to move onwards to new focuses!

author: embirico
text:
7/8: Downstream results
- As usual, the PH & press signups are less engaged than organic traffic
- For example, our macOS install rate is ~40%
- That's ok as long as it climbs, which it usually does

author: embirico
text:
5/8: Thoughts on perf cont.
- Could be that our experiment of marketing a niche, consumery feature (Spotify sync) instead of main product (virtual office) didn't pay off
- Or maybe the payoff will be more spread out from press coverage. We'll know more in a week

author: embirico
text:
4/8: Thoughts on performance
- The lowest performing of our 3 launches so far
- We expected lower results because we held off on the multiple emails, DMs etc to rally community to PH. But this is still lower than our lowered baseline

Now today we’ve come a surprising full circle, and office hours is one of the gateway use cases for Remotion.
Teams who are onboarding new hires quickly find them invaluable.

author: embirico
text:
“Office hours for remote teams”
A few years ago when @potatoarecool and I started market research for Remotion, we found a few failed products for this.
It seemed like there was a need, but not enough for a new product.

author: embirico
text:
Our take:

Talent attracts talent. People come to work energized by their teammates.

The value of the watercooler is a place where in-person teams get to know each other and get energized.

Remotion is building the place where distributed teams do the same.
(2/2)

author: embirico
text:
Good chat with @trondau, who asked existential questions like, paraphrasing, "Why try to reproduce office dynamics for remote teams? Why not accept they're different?"

At @remotionco we talk to teams who want to recreate "the watercooler" remotely and we ask them the same.
(1/2)

author: embirico
text:
@stroughtonsmith IMO the decline in Apple-made macOS software is less a macOS skills gap and more
- Shift in primary application of desktop (vs mobile) towards work & prosumer
- Work & prosumer apps increasingly cloud-based
- Apple not great at cloud applications (or clients for those)

@adityaag Fav Q: “On a scale of 0-10, what’s it like working with this person?”

Response isn’t used for calibration, but you’ll rarely hear “10.”

Then ask: “What would take this person to a 10?”

And listen carefully to the constructive thoughts you’ve trapped them into sharing!

text:
@jmitch Agreed... but only at first:
1. Write doc
2. Someone asks you instead of reading doc (if private DM, ask to repost Q publicly)
3. You reply with link to doc in public channel + ask them to edit if unclear
4. Repeat a few times
5. Team knows doc and you are no longer gatekeeper ⭐️
